title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1982-04-06
lineage: Dat -> Samplitude Professional v10.22 -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> FLAC/16

ai_review.summary: A superb spring‑'82 soundboard capture with buttery clarity, highlighted by a smoking Shakedown Street opener, intense Other One → Morning Dew, and tight, high‑energy jams throughout.
ai_review.review: The SBD source is praised for its smooth, fat mix that lets Phil’s funky bass and Jerry’s on‑fire guitar shine, while Brent’s keyboards trade playful licks with the lead. Standout moments include Shakedown Street, the Other One into Morning Dew, Jack‑A‑Roe and a tight Terrapin Station bridge, all delivered at a high‑energy level that many fans call one of the best early‑’80s shows.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 5 stars, noting excellent performance and superb soundboard quality; only a few low‑star outliers mention minor issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as smooth, buttery, fat, and the best SBD of early ’82; occasional mentions of minor dropouts but no major flaws.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds with tight, warm playing; second set launches with a fiery Shakedown opener and maintains high momentum through extended jams and seamless transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly called 'on fire' with great solos (Terrapin bridge, Other One), playful trading licks with Brent, and a tight guitar tone.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted as more prevalent in the mix and particularly funky for this era; his bass drives many jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocals noted on The Other One (first verse only) and his rhythm work supports the high‑energy flow.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s keyboards highlighted for playful exchanges with Jerry, slide practice moments, and overall strong presence.
band_member_comments.Drums: Described as solid and dynamic, especially on the second‑set drum segment.
